title: Serre's quasi-compact vanishing criterion
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Assume that $X$ is quasi-compact and that $H^1(X,\mathcal I)=0$ for every quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ [pqf-def-coherent, pqf-def-cohomology]. Then $X$ is affine.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma Tag 01XF (label lemma-quasi-compact-h1-zero-covering), lines 283-388

proof.text: Fix a closed point $x\in X$ and an affine open neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $x$, with $\mathfrak m\subset A$ the maximal ideal corresponding to $x$. Put $Z=X\setminus U$ and $Z'=Z\cup\{x\}$; both are closed because $x$ is a closed point. Let $\mathcal I=\mathcal I_Z$ and $\mathcal I'=\mathcal I_{Z'}$ be the quasi-coherent ideal sheaves of the reduced induced closed subschemes on $Z$ and $Z'$ [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]; since $Z\subseteq Z'$, the defining vanishing condition gives $\mathcal I'\subseteq\mathcal I$. By part (1) of that lemma, on $U$ they are $\widetilde I$ and $\widetilde{I'}$ for the radical ideals with $V(I)=Z\cap U=\emptyset$ and $V(I')=\{x\}$, i.e. $I=A$ and $I'=\mathfrak m$; so $(\mathcal I/\mathcal I')|_U\cong\widetilde{A/\mathfrak m}$. On the open $X\setminus\{x\}$ one has $Z\cap(X\setminus\{x\})=Z'\cap(X\setminus\{x\})$, so $\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal I'$ agree there and $\mathcal I/\mathcal I'$ is supported at $x$. Since $U$ and $X\setminus\{x\}$ cover $X$, $\Gamma(X,\mathcal I/\mathcal I')=\Gamma(U,\mathcal I/\mathcal I')=A/\mathfrak m$. Apply the long exact cohomology sequence to $0\to\mathcal I'\to\mathcal I\to\mathcal I/\mathcal I'\to0$ [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact]: the hypothesis $H^1(X,\mathcal I')=0$ makes $\Gamma(X,\mathcal I)\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal I/\mathcal I')$ surjective, so $1\in A/\mathfrak m$ lifts to $f\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal I)\subseteq\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. Its image $f_A\in A$ is not in $\mathfrak m$, so $x\in X_f$; and $f(z)=0$ for $z\in Z$, so $X_f\subseteq U$. Hence $X_f=D(f_A)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$ is affine.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma Tag 01XF, proof lines 323-352

proof.text: Let $W$ be the union of all $X_f$, $f\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, with $X_f$ affine. It is open and contains every closed point of $X$ by Step 1. If $X\setminus W$ were nonempty, it would be a closed subset of the quasi-compact space $X$, which is Kolmogorov since $X$ is a scheme, so it would contain a point closed in $X$ [lem-sc-quasi-compact-kolmogorov-closed-point], contradicting that all closed points lie in $W$. Thus $W=X$, and by quasi-compactness there are $f_1,\dots,f_n\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ with $X=X_{f_1}\cup\dots\cup X_{f_n}$ and each $X_{f_i}$ affine.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma Tag 01XF, proof lines 353-364

proof.text: The sections $f_1,\dots,f_n$ define $\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal O_X$, $e_i\mapsto f_i$, which is surjective: at each point some $f_i$ is a unit in the stalk because the $X_{f_i}$ cover $X$. Let $\mathcal F$ be its kernel (quasi-coherent) and $\mathcal F_i=\mathcal F\cap(\mathcal O_X^{\oplus i}\oplus0^{\oplus(n-i)})$, so $0=\mathcal F_0\subseteq\mathcal F_1\subseteq\dots\subseteq\mathcal F_n=\mathcal F$. Projection to the $i$-th summand identifies $\mathcal F_i/\mathcal F_{i-1}$ with a quasi-coherent subsheaf of $\mathcal O_X$, i.e. a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals, so $H^1(X,\mathcal F_i/\mathcal F_{i-1})=0$ by hypothesis. By induction on $i$, the long exact sequence of $0\to\mathcal F_{i-1}\to\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal F_i/\mathcal F_{i-1}\to0$ [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] gives the exact segment $H^1(X,\mathcal F_{i-1})\to H^1(X,\mathcal F_i)\to H^1(X,\mathcal F_i/\mathcal F_{i-1})$ with both ends zero, hence $H^1(X,\mathcal F_i)=0$; in particular $H^1(X,\mathcal F)=0$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma Tag 01XF, proof lines 365-378

proof.text: The long exact cohomology sequence of $0\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal O_X\to0$ [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] and $H^1(X,\mathcal F)=0$ make $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)^{\oplus n}\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, $(a_i)\mapsto\sum a_if_i$, surjective. Therefore $f_1,\dots,f_n$ generate the unit ideal of $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma Tag 01XF, proof lines 375-388

proof.text: Apply the affine criterion [lem-weil-pbc-affine-unit-ideal-basic-opens] to $f_1,\dots,f_n$, which generate the unit ideal of $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ (Step 4) and have affine $X_{f_i}$ (Step 2): $X$ is affine.
